entries.meaning: How dusty the sky is. Bigger number = more dust = less sunlight.
One Mars day. It is about 40 minutes longer than a day on Earth.
A flat panel that turns sunlight into electricity.
Stores power so you can use it later, even at night.
The part of air your body needs to breathe.
Invisible energy from the Sun and space. Too much is not safe for people.
How much radiation your body got in total.
Walls or material that block radiation, like a sun umbrella for your body.
Step-by-step instructions written ahead of time for an emergency.
When the Sun is between Mars and Earth, so radio messages can't get through.
Going outside in your spacesuit. It stands for extra-vehicular activity.
Tiny grey balls of a mineral called hematite that Opportunity found at Meridiani. They formed in water long ago.
The team on Earth that watches over a space mission and sends advice by radio.
Loose, fluffy sand. Rover wheels dig in and spin instead of moving.
Glowing lights in the sky, made when particles from the Sun hit the air.
The pull that keeps you on the ground. Mars pulls about a third as hard as Earth.
Radio messages take minutes to travel between Mars and Earth, so answers come late.
